body.statement:
For every data-generating member of
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\),
\(\Pr\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}\ge1-\alpha\). The claim holds without
selecting a matrix-root branch and without divided-difference or
branch-separation assumptions. If an observed moment law has two compatible
members of the compact class with unequal queried transfers, then the set
need not contract: whenever the common moment pair is in
\(\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\), both attained transfers belong to
\(\mathcal C_n^h\).
body.justification: Inverse-image coverage is the globally valid counterpart to local branchwise Wald inference.
body.gap: The cited process-graph inference paper conditions on a differentiable fine-grid effect and does not cover observationally equivalent roots or singular fibers.
body.consumer: Scientific conclusions remain valid when sampling parity, persistence collisions, or finite samples leave several fine-grid causal explanations alive.
body.proof_tex:
Let the true compact-class member be denoted by \((A_\star,D_\star)\), and
let its stationary coarse moments be \((M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\). On the
event
\[
 E_n=\{(M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\},
\]
the coarse-law reduction gives
\[
 M_{1\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star},
 \qquad
 M_{0\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star}(A_\star^m)^\top
 +\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_\star^rD_\star(A_\star^r)^\top.
\]
It also gives \(M_{0\star}\succ0\). Every remaining constraint in the
definition of \(\mathcal R_n\) is exactly one of the triangularity, graph
support, stability-margin, entry-envelope, diagonality, or innovation
eigenvalue conditions defining the compact class. Consequently,
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{(A_\star,D_\star)\in\mathcal R_n\}.
\]
For every \(|z|=1\), the denominator in the transfer is nonzero because
\[
 |1-(A_\star)_{vv}z|\ge1-| (A_\star)_{vv}|
 \ge\gamma>0.
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal C_n^h\) now implies
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}.
\]
The uniform moment-box theorem gives \(\Pr(E_n)\ge1-\alpha\), proving the
coverage statement. This argument quantifies over all compatible
\((A,D)\) simultaneously and nowhere chooses a root branch or divides by a
divided difference.

For the noncontraction assertion, suppose two compact-class members
\((A^{(1)},D^{(1)})\) and \((A^{(2)},D^{(2)})\) generate the same moment
pair and satisfy \(h_{uv}^{(1)}\ne h_{uv}^{(2)}\). Repeating the preceding
membership argument for both members shows that on the single event that
their common moment pair lies in the moment box, both transfers lie in
\(\mathcal C_n^h\). In particular, in the supremum norm on
\(\mathbb T\), the diameter is at least
\(\lVert h_{uv}^{(1)}-h_{uv}^{(2)}\rVert_\infty>0\) on an event of
probability at least \(1-\alpha\), for every \(n\).

Such behavior is attained within the stated structural model whenever the
queried arrow \(u\to v\) is allowed by \(G\). Choose
\(0<c<L\), choose \(\lambda\in(d_{\min},d_{\max})\), put
\[
 A^{(1)}=c e_ve_u^\top,
 \qquad A^{(2)}=-c e_ve_u^\top,
 \qquad D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}=\lambda I_d.
\]
Because \(u\ne v\), both transition matrices square to zero. Thus, for every
\(m\ge2\), both models have
\[
 B=0,
 \qquad
 Q=\lambda I_d+\lambda c^2e_ve_v^\top,
\]
and hence the same
\((M_0,M_1)=(Q,0)\), while their transfers are respectively \(cz\) and
\(-cz\). Their diagonal entries vanish, so the stability margin holds; all
support, envelope, positivity, and innovation bounds hold by construction.
This is an explicit interior, transfer-distinct witness to possible
noncontraction.
